subject: mathematics
question_text: If a = i − 2j − 3k, b = 2i + j − k and c = i + 3j − 2k, find a × (b × c).

mark_split.label: Find b × c, the vector in the bracket

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.69, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 10. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 2+2 split gives half the marks to the inner bracket and half to the outer product, because each one is a complete 3 × 3 determinant expansion and a student who does only one has done half the work. CHECKED THREE WAYS: b × c = i + 3j + 5k dotted with b gives 2 + 3 − 5 = 0 and with c gives 1 + 9 − 10 = 0; a × (b × c) = −i − 8j + 5k dotted with a gives −1 + 16 − 15 = 0 and with b × c gives −1 − 24 + 25 = 0; and the expansion formula a × (b × c) = (a·c)b − (a·b)c with a·c = 1 and a·b = 3 gives b − 3c = −i − 8j + 5k, the same vector. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies at least one of those eight on almost every paper. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would work out this triple product — say which product you do first and why.

steps.label: Find b × c
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Put b on the second row and c on the third, in the order the bracket names them. Swapping those two rows reverses the sign of the whole answer.
steps.memory_tip: Row order copies the bracket: b on the second row, c on the third.
lines: Given a = i − 2j − 3k, b = 2i + j − k
The bracket is worked out first.

recall.must_convey: That the bracket b × c is evaluated first and equals i + 3j + 5k.
accept: do the bracket first so b cross c is i plus three j plus five k
b cross c comes out as i plus three j plus five k
evaluate the inner cross product before the outer one
modata bracket lo b cross c cheyyali, i plus three j plus five k
the inner product gives i plus three j plus five k

steps.why: The outer cross product cannot start until the bracket has been reduced to a single vector, so b × c is done first. This is the same rule as doing brackets first in ordinary algebra.
common_mistakes: Crossing a with b first because a is written first.
Dropping the minus sign that stands in front of the j term.

steps.label: Cross a into that result
steps.margin_note: The other half. a goes on the second row because the product is written a × (…). The answer must be perpendicular to a, so dot it with a and look for 0.
steps.memory_tip: a sits above the bracket result, matching the order a × (b × c) is written in.

recall.must_convey: That a is crossed into the bracket result, with a on the upper row, giving −i − 8j + 5k.
accept: cross a with that vector keeping a on top to get minus i minus eight j plus five k
the answer is minus i minus eight j plus five k
put a on the second row and the bracket result on the third
a ni pai row lo petti cross cheste minus i minus eight j plus five k
the final vector is minus i minus eight j plus five k

steps.why: Reversing a cross product reverses its sign, so a must stay on the upper row. The result is perpendicular to a, and dotting it with a to get 0 catches a sign error in two lines.
common_mistakes: Putting the bracket result above a, which negates the answer.
Sign slip in the j term of the second determinant.
